title: One year later: Here is how Barrie police and county paramedics have responded to the coroner's inquest recommendations into Olando Brown's death
subtitle: The arrest of Olando Brown was a high-profile incident that generated protests after he accidentally died in police custody.
article: A year after a coroner's inquest into the custody-related death of a Barrie man, the agencies involved say they are working their way through the recommendations.

In March 2024, a jury looking at the death of 32-year-old Olando Brown made 16 recommendations , with nine directed at the County of Simcoe either alone, or in combination with Barrie police and Barrie fire. Recommendations made during a coroner's inquest are not mandatory.
Brown choked to death in 2018 while in the custody of the Barrie Police Service.

The inquest heard that paramedics first on the scene were aware Brown had an airway blockage, but during the heightened panic, an advanced care paramedic arriving later did not realize it until minutes had passed. Even though the advanced care paramedic had specialized tools to look for a blockage, they weren't used. Instead, Brown was treated for cardiac arrest.
The coroner's inquest jury labelled Brown's death as "accidental."

Many of the recommendations that came from Brown's inquest were tied to communication protocols, and standards and training - including cross-training between the Barrie Police Service and county paramedics.
That included developing best practices for police officers regarding the information that should be communicated to ambulance dispatch when requesting paramedic services.
Barrie police spokesperson Peter Leon said his agency is working through the inquest recommendations with the other parties.

"We have worked with and will continue to work with the County of Simcoe Paramedics, Barrie Fire and Emergency Services and the County of Simcoe to ensure all recommendations are covered," he wrote in an email.

Since the inquest, according to Barrie police's response to regional coroner David Cameron on its followup to the jury's recommendations, the service has created a new procedure related to passing information on to paramedics. Additionally, the service is working with county paramedics on a two-person team - one paramedic and one mental health worker - who would respond to certain calls.

"Barrie Police Service is open to an invitation to partake in any training opportunities," the letter to the coroner read, noting the service "regularly" conducts scenario-based training with paramedics.

In an email, Jane Sinclair, the county's general manager of health and emergency services, stated that after a careful review of the findings related to paramedic service, "we have taken proactive steps to address each recommendation through continued education sessions."

Last November, the service launched a new ambulance dispatch system which she said addresses issues highlighted through the inquest process, including how and when advanced care paramedics are assigned to calls.

The county did not respond to the request to update the coroner's office on the status of the recommendations directed to the paramedic service, according to the Office of the Chief Coroner. The county it did not receive the request from the coroner.
An autopsy of Olando Brown determined he choked to death on two bags of narcotics he attempted to swallow during a strip search while in custody of Barrie Police, June 22, 2018 .
Health Canada later concluded the bags contained heroin, fentanyl, caffeine and dimethylsulphone.
The province's Special Investigations Unit cleared city officers of wrongdoing .
Brown's arrest by Barrie Police in the downtown was captured by video, raising concerns that it was heavy-handed.

The video, which is no longer online, purported to show two officers grabbing Brown and telling him to stop resisting while they force him to the ground. The officers used "on body" Taser shots to subdue Brown. A third officer also joined in to hold him down.
A protest was held in downtown Barrie three days after his death in response to the manner in which Brown was arrested.
